title: R and comma
summary: Two new keys: R and comma. The finger goes out, presses, and comes back.
intro: Two new keys in this lesson: R and comma. They belong to your right ring finger and your left ring finger. The movement is always the same — out, press, back — and the way back is the part being trained, because a finger left out of place spoils the next letter.
congrats: Two more keys under your fingers. If R and comma already come without searching, the lesson has done its job.

screens.text: This key belongs to your right ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only R and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.

r r rr
rrrr
rrrrrr rrrrrr

screens.text: This key belongs to your left ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only , and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
Short groups, one after another. Keep going to the end even if you miss one.
The new keys mixed with the old ones, which is how they will turn up inside words.

screens.text: Real words with the new keys. Type each word in one go, not letter by letter.

Now the weight is on R, the one you have pressed least.

Everything you have, mixed together. Notice how many words already come without thinking.
